This pack adds a "Glow" slider (0-24px) that drives an accent halo on the clock and on the search bar when it is focused. It leaves your colours, layout and widgets untouched. At 0 the glow disappears.

```json
{
  "kind": "mnt.theme-pack",
  "packVersion": 2,
  "cssApiVersion": 1,
  "variables": [
    {
      "name": "--glow",
      "label": { "en": "Accent glow", "zh-CN": "强调色光晕" },
      "type": "range",
      "min": 0,
      "max": 24,
      "unit": "px",
      "default": 10
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "name": "Accent glow",
    "description": "A soft accent-coloured glow around the clock and the focused search bar, adjustable from 0 to 24px.",
    "notes": "No wallpaper needed; a dark, low-detail image works best if you add one."
  },
  "css": ".mnt-clock {\n  text-shadow: 0 0 var(--glow, 10px) color-mix(in srgb, var(--mnt-accent) 70%, transparent);\n}\n.mnt-search:focus-within {\n  border-color: var(--mnt-accent);\n  box-shadow: 0 0 var(--glow, 10px) color-mix(in srgb, var(--mnt-accent) 60%, transparent);\n}\n@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {\n  .mnt-search {\n    transition: box-shadow var(--mnt-dur-base) var(--mnt-ease), border-color var(--mnt-dur-base) var(--mnt-ease);\n  }\n}"
}
```

The CSS reads `--glow` directly, assuming the extension supplies the value with its `px` unit. If the preview shows no glow, the value is probably unitless, and you can ask me to switch the CSS to `calc(var(--glow) * 1px)`.
